title: Check fenders and integrated lights
summary: Inspect the wet-weather hardware that makes an everyday utility bike practical without confusing equipment checks with legal certification.

steps.title: Check both fenders for wheel clearance
steps.instruction: Spin both wheels and watch the fenders and stays. Look for rubbing, loose mounts, deformation or anything that could contact the tire.
steps.why: A fender sits close to a moving wheel, so looseness or deformation can become an interference problem.
steps.warning: Do not ride if a loose or damaged fender can contact or jam a wheel.
steps.check: Both fenders remain clear of the tires through wheel rotation.

steps.title: Clean the light lenses
steps.instruction: Wipe dirt or water film from the front and rear light lenses and inspect the housings/mounts for obvious damage.
steps.why: Integrated lights can only work effectively when their lenses and mounts are in usable condition.
steps.check: Both lenses are clean enough to inspect and the housings appear secure.

steps.title: Confirm both lights actually operate
steps.instruction: Activate the bicycle's real lighting system and confirm front and rear lights operate consistently through the modes you intend to use.
steps.why: Being physically present on the bicycle is not the same as being powered and functional.
steps.warning: Required lighting equipment and use rules vary by jurisdiction. This functional check is not a legal-compliance certification.
steps.check: The intended front and rear lighting functions operate consistently.

steps.title: Recheck moving-part clearance
steps.instruction: With the bicycle stationary and then during a controlled low-speed roll, listen for rubbing and confirm fenders, lights, wiring and mounts cannot enter the wheels or steering path.
steps.why: Utility hardware is useful only when it remains safely separated from moving parts.
steps.warning: Stop if any accessory can interfere with a wheel, steering or braking component.
steps.check: The utility hardware remains secure and clear during the controlled check.
